description:
Mission Control, calling future astronauts!

The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer turns space science into a game that any kid can play. Pick a mission, pass the training levels, earn your badges and blast off!
summary:
Lunar Outpost Academy turns lunar exploration into a guided mission for children ages 7–12. Players choose one of six real Apollo landing sites, mapped with NASA coordinates, then drive a rover through a training route: scan three survey points in order and reach the beacon to unlock the habitat mission.

In mission control, players balance air, power and radiation shielding with simple actions: refresh air, charge batteries, strengthen protection or shelter the crew. Each day brings tradeoffs, points and a chance to recover and try a new strategy.

Captain Luna explains every control with step-by-step narration, highlighted focus cues and replay, previous and skip options. No account is needed, and names, progress and scores are saved locally.

Live NASA DONKI space-weather data adds real solar-storm warnings, while NASA archive photos and clearly labelled simulations separate observed facts from gameplay.

Children learn engineering by making decisions, seeing effects and reflecting, not just memorising facts. By pairing approachable play with traceable science, the game makes planetary exploration understandable and meaningful. Built with React, Three.js and Tailwind CSS, and deployed on Vercel.
details:
Lunar Outpost Academy is a browser-based learning game that introduces children to the challenges of exploring and living on the Moon. Players choose among six real Apollo landing sites, guide a rover along an illustrated training route, and then manage a lunar habitat by balancing air, power, and radiation protection. The game combines Apollo location information, NASA imagery, and space-weather data with clearly labeled simulated gameplay.

It works through a sequence of interactive tasks: players select a destination, scan route points with the rover, and make choices in mission control. Narration and visual guidance help explain what to do, while feedback, points, and mission progress show how decisions affect the crew.

The project aims to build curiosity about space and introduce systems thinking, planning, and problem-solving through play. Its creative element is connecting real lunar exploration information to a guided rover challenge and habitat-management game, rather than presenting space facts as a quiz.

It is built with JavaScript, React, CSS, Vite, Zustand, and Motion. It runs in a web browser without an account or app download. Accessibility-minded features include narration controls, keyboard movement, clear instructions, and options to skip or revisit guidance; the experience has not been formally accessibility-certified. The game uses public NASA resources and open-source tools, so there is no required app purchase, though internet access and any hosting costs may apply.
